clue.text: Agreement — it could be in the bag

definitions.meaning: a pact or formal deal between parties

definitions.text: it could be in the bag
definitions.meaning: a small case of face powder with a mirror, carried in a handbag

explanation.surface: A deal is as good as done, safely in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the bag' looks like the idiom for a done deal, but it is literal: the powder case sits in a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for a treaty, and also the name of a pocket make-up case with mirror and powder.

clue.text: Mostly pink but black-hearted creature

indicators.note: black-hearted reads as the letter for black placed at the heart of the other piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A creature that looks pretty in pink but has a wicked heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black-hearted' looks like a description of a villain; split it and it puts B inside CORA (CORAL with its last letter dropped, from 'Mostly').
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous hooded snake is one example of a creature.

clue.text: Model German writer seen on horse briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece seen on another sits above it

parts.note: Thomas Mann, author of Death in Venice

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an equine is a horse or member of the horse family

explanation.surface: A model posing for a German author, perched briefly on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims EQUINE to EQUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy figure used to display clothes in a shop is a model.

clue.text: Circumnavigating pole, surprisingly unnamed Norwegian explorer

indicators.note: going right round, so the rearranged letters go around the pole's letter
surprisingly signals the letters of the following word come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole (or south as a magnetic pole)

explanation.surface: An anonymous Norwegian explorer, surprisingly, sails round the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges UNNAMED into AMUNDEN, which 'Circumnavigating' puts around S.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen, first to reach the South Pole in 1911, was a famous Norwegian polar explorer.

clue.text: Carry child on back of bike

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Carrying a child on the back of a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug or haul something along is to carry it.

clue.text: Springfield's beer: drink mugs?

definitions.note: a verb: attacks and roughs up someone

parts.note: Duff is the beer drunk in Springfield in The Simpsons
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson's beer, drunk from mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' looks like beer glasses but is the verb meaning assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating someone up, the slang phrasal verb, is what a mugger does to a victim.

clue.text: Took one of two Scrabble tiles and made no further progress

definitions.text: Took one of two Scrabble tiles
definitions.meaning: a Scrabble set holds two letterless wildcard tiles; picking one from the bag
failed to find anything, got nowhere

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player picks a tile and gets stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally pulling a letterless wildcard tile, and idiomatically failing to find what you sought.

clue.text: Film, lightweight, shown in French (children missed out)

indicators.note: one piece shown inside another is placed within it
the children's abbreviation is omitted from the word

parts.note: taken as written
an ounce, OZ, is a light weight

explanation.surface: A film shown in French, with children not admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed out' sounds like a cinema age rule, but it drops the children's abbreviation from the word for French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney animated hit of 2013 is a film.

clue.text: Small vegetable? Right, asparagus for example

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Someone asks if asparagus counts as a small vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asparagus for example' defines by example: an asparagus shoot is a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shoot of asparagus is called a spear, so asparagus gives an example.

clue.text: Pottery is laid out for people coming later

indicators.note: laid out means the letters are set out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pottery set out on display for future generations.
explanation.definitionFit: Future generations, those who come after us, are collectively one's descendants.

clue.text: After sumptuous meal, drink without a place to sit

indicators.note: the drink's letters come after the meal's

parts.note: a banquet is a lavish feast

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: After a feast, having a drink with nowhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a place to sit' reads as a single phrase, but 'without a' belongs to the drink and only 'place to sit' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered bench along a wall, as in restaurants, is a seat.

clue.text: Launches competitions welcoming all-comers

definitions.meaning: tournaments, as in golf and tennis, open to amateurs and professionals alike

explanation.surface: A new tournament launches with entry open to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, starts things; as a noun, tournaments with unrestricted entry such as the British golf championship.

clue.text: Commander introduces final list of discussion items

indicators.note: the commander takes in the other word, which goes inside

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A commander brings out the final list of items for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA, an Ottoman commander, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The programme of business for a meeting is its agenda, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Imprisoned by Native Americans, a judge is relaxed

indicators.note: the article and judge are held inside the tribe's name

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
a referee judges a game

explanation.surface: A judge held captive by Native Americans stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' is a sports referee, REF, not a court judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Untroubled and easy-going is a synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: Football team's problem, wearing cotton fabric

indicators.note: the fabric is worn around the problem, so it encloses it

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton cloth
an ill is a problem or misfortune

explanation.surface: A football team's kit trouble: they're stuck in cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillingham FC is an English football club in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillingham FC, known as the Gills, is a professional English soccer club.

clue.text: Possibly valued live theatrical entertainment

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Live theatre that one might value.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety shows of songs, comedy and acts, the American music-hall tradition, are stage entertainment.

clue.text: Pistol flare extremely easy to transport

parts.note: very means extremely
something light is easy to carry about

explanation.surface: A flare pistol that's extremely easy to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The flare is named after its inventor, Edward Very, an American naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured signal flare fired from a special pistol bears this name.

clue.text: Bear a teacher of well-being

definitions.meaning: the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park
a master of yoga who teaches its practice

explanation.surface: A bear who teaches well-being.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanna-Barbera cartoon bear, and a Hindu master of yoga and meditation.

clue.text: Hoping for profit? Taken home, after going bust

indicators.note: something going bust breaks apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business, after going bust, is taken home in the hope of profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone ambitiously out for personal gain or advantage.

clue.text: Small dog having sickly joints, might you say?

indicators.note: says the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: peaky means sickly and the knees are joints

explanation.surface: A small dog with sickly joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peaky' is British for looking pale and unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy breed from China, flat-faced and long-haired, is a small dog.

clue.text: Band leader in group hugs

indicators.note: the phrase hugs the answer, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: A band leader gives the group hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band leader' looks like one phrase; 'Band' alone is the definition, and 'leader' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular band, such as one worn on a finger, is a synonym.

clue.text: Don't make rough suggestions in a mournful voice

definitions.meaning: split into two words, it means propose schemes softly
with a sad, resonant, plaintive sound

explanation.surface: Advice to speak softly and sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'plan gently' is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes a plaintive, melancholy resonance, as of bells or a lament.

clue.text: In assortments we discovered gobstoppers, say

indicators.note: the word we goes in the assortments
found, as the pronoun is discovered within

parts.note: sets are assortments or collections

explanation.surface: Among assortments, we found gobstoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: A gobstopper is a very large hard round sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobstoppers are one example of confectionery, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Socialist newspaper anticipating victory secured by Liberal, say

indicators.note: the paper and victory are held within the other letters

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: coming before, so the newspaper precedes the victory

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A socialist paper looks forward to a Liberal win.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes into EG, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialist politics sits on the political left, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Plants I'd exported from American state

indicators.note: sent out of the state, so the letters are removed

parts.note: Florida is a US state

explanation.surface: Plants I had shipped out of an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective plant life of a region is its flora.

clue.text: Criminal ironed what could be laundered in America?

definitions.text: what could be laundered in America?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A criminal ironing clothes, and laundering in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ironed' and 'laundered' suggest washing; it is money-laundering.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish-derived slang for money in the US; crooks launder cash.

clue.text: Piece of recondite gossip in French

indicators.note: a piece of the word gives the answer as a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A piece of obscure gossip, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally 'it is said' means a rumour or piece of hearsay.

clue.text: Attack magistrate without hesitation

indicators.note: without means outside, so the magistrate's letters go around

parts.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace
um is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Attack the magistrate without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone suddenly is to attack them.

clue.text: London theatre in the round?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's playhouse on the South Bank
a sphere is a round thing

explanation.surface: A London theatre that stages plays in the round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the round' looks like the staging term; 'the round' is just a ball shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's reconstructed Bankside playhouse; also a spherical body like the earth.

clue.text: In short, home help could accept employment … as this?

definitions.text: In short, home help could accept employment … as this?

indicators.note: the other letters take in the employment word

parts.note: HO is a short form of house or home
a maid is a domestic help
use is employment of something

explanation.surface: A home help taking a job could become one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant doing household chores is a home help taking up employment.

clue.text: Beam finally put at front of restored manors

indicators.note: the single letter goes before the rest
finally means take the last letter
restored means the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A beam is finally put in at the front of restored manor houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges MANORS into RANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal crossbar above a door or window is a beam.

clue.text: Former girlfriend with fairly short clothing makes excuse

indicators.note: the shortened word clothes the former partner, going round it
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: pretty means fairly, as in pretty good
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex in rather skimpy clothing makes an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly short clothing' suggests a skimpy outfit, but 'fairly' is the synonym being shortened and 'clothing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason given to hide the real one is an excuse.
